title: Tenant-level journal pruning and adaptive slab throttle to stop multi-modal GPU OOM cascade
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported GPU OOM cascades over the last week. Root cause triage points to a slow-growing tenant-scoped journal growth combined with fragmentation in the slab allocator and a KV cache handle leak under certain long-lived sessions. When journal growth crosses a per-GPU working set threshold it triggers aggressive allocator preemption which amplifies fragmentation and leads to OOMs across colocated tenants.

This ticket tracks a two-part runtime patch: (1) a tenant-level journal pruning agent that enforces soft quotas and opportunistic compaction, plus a prune-on-idle path for sessions that have low activity; (2) an adaptive slab throttle that temporarily tightens per-tenant slab allocations and triggers faster epochal compaction when pressure is detected. The fix is intended to be fast-rolling with canaries on Hosted, smoke on Dedicated, and a controlled release artifact for Private (upgrade bundle).
proposed_solution: Implement a background journal_prune agent that records per-tenant journal high-water marks and attempts incremental compaction when the per-GPU working set (journal + active KV handles) exceeds configured thresholds. Add fast-path prune-on-idle logic for session termination and a bounded length journal journal_index that can be truncated after checkpointing. In parallel implement an adaptive_slab_throttle which reduces per-tenant slab inflight growth factor and initiates an immediate compaction pass when alloc failure rate exceeds X per-minute. Both features expose runtime flags to allow zero-downtime rollback.
mitigation_actions: 2026-03-10 03:42 UTC:Scoped supervised restart of affected Dedicated pool (manual drain + warm restart) — temporary relief for impacted customers
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC: Applied emergency KV handle GC in hosted canary to reclaim stale session handles — reduced OOM rate by ~60% for canary hosts
2026-03-11 11:20 UTC: Deployed per-tenant soft quota rule via edge routing to limit max concurrent open sessions for largest tenants (stopgap)
Ongoing: customers with Private deployments given interim patch bundle and instructions to enable kvcache monitoring (see attachments)
test_plan: Unit tests for journal index truncation, verify durability invariants under simulated checkpoint failures
Integration test: reproduce kv-handle leak pattern with long-lived sessions + synthetic traffic, verify prune agent reclaims 95% of orphaned journal entries within 10 minutes
Load test: Dedicated pool run with 100 tenants, ramp active sessions until slab fragmentation grows; verify adaptive slab throttle keeps OOMs <1% and latency SLO impact <5%
Canary rollout on Hosted: 5% traffic for 2 hours, validate no regression on generation latency and token throughput
rollback_plan: Feature flags gate both journal_prune and adaptive_slab_throttle. Rollback by toggling flags off via config service and gradually draining canary hosts; if immediate rollback insufficient, revert runtime binary to previous build (runtime-1.20) and perform controlled restart on canaries before broad rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canary pass: zero new OOM incidents in canary group for 48h under representative load
Dedicated smoke: no >P99 latency regression and no tenant-level OOMs during smoke run
Host metrics: per-GPU working set 95th percentile reduced by >=20% for previously impacted hosts
Post-deploy automated regression alert for kvcache-leak patterns is enabled
